findings.reason: without a stated carve-out (or a convention-free entry point) a §3 node either invents a call for a reader with no translation to perform or records a pass its search cannot show.
findings.text: §3(2) requires that "every census reader calls the §2 entry point", but the census's reader table includes the flux-loop and probe readers `nova/imas/magnetics.py::Magnetics.flux_loop` and `nova/imas/io_magnetics.py::Magnetics`, which read sensor identity and geometry and for which the census states no digits are derivable and that "the choice is §2's" (pass them through convention-free, or declare a convention at each boundary); §2 landed only `nova/io/sourcemap.py::translate_equilibrium`, which takes equilibrium observables (`ip`, `psi_axis`, `psi_boundary`, `q`, `b0`) and returns a `SourceSignalMap`, and `nova/io/sourcemap.py` contains no reference to magnetics, flux loops or probes, so those readers have no §2 entry point to call and the clause cannot be satisfied as written

findings.reason: a one-line classification of `extrapolate.py` as an internal consumer is needed before the check keys on a zero-hit search over readers.
findings.text: §3(2) treats "any reader" as a set its rerun of §1's sign search can show empty, but the census's IDS-reader table carries the row `nova/imas/extrapolate.py::Extrapolate.update` ("Reader of the row above") while the plan's §3 body and §4 both put that file's `# COCOS` literals (`extrapolate.py:301`, `:345`) in §4's writer/internal-consumer set, so the search returns two live hits in a file the census calls a reader and the node cannot tell whether to clear them or defer them; the mechanism and the measure disagree on which section owns a named site

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `nova/imas/plasma_source.py` exists with a guard at line 76, its `PlasmaSource.from_imas` classmethod exists (plasma_source.py:181) and is the row the census lists (`docs/research/dd-cocos-census.html:32`), and iter-passive-plasma-circuit §6 resolves with CORSICA 130506/6 as its provisional reference.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — the changed clause of §3(1) is sound (refusing DINA 105013/1 beside 105014/1, each with its contradicting digit, matches §2's landed refusal on σ_ρθφ), but §3(1) has no statement of the path the refusal comes from, and §3(2) requires *every* census reader to call the §2 entry point, which the census's own convention-free geometry readers cannot do.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §3 names no scratch path; its checks write to the readers' own test files and its search counts are reproducible commands, so nothing durable is left in a temporary directory.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §3 introduces no symbol, file or comment carrying a plan label, stage name or ticket number.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §3(2) asserts a search can be shown to find no `# COCOS` sign site in any reader, but the census's IDS-reader table lists `nova/imas/extrapolate.py::Extrapolate.update`, whose `# COCOS` literals §3 and §4 both assign to §4.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §3 carries one deliverable, that the census readers route their reads through the §2 translator and the plasma-source guard retires.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — s3 declares `dd-cocos-ingest#s2` in both the plan-level `plan-section-depends-on` map and its own `data-links`, and §2 is the translator it consumes; no other edge is owed by s3.
